# d0nj plugins for DeepSeek Harness
A collection of Cordis bundles for DeepSeek Harness, managed as a Turborepo monorepo.
Each package is a `dsh` bundle: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its `package.json`, and installing
it adds plugin rows to a profile. The Harness loads built JavaScript from `dist/`, so the TypeScrip
t here is compiled before installation.
## Packages
| Package | What it adds |
| `@d0nj/dsh-websearch-multi` | Thirteen `web_search` backends and four `web_fetch` backends behind

the existing `ctx.web` seam. |
| `@d0nj/dsh-ui-custom` | Theme presets, colour tokens, typography an

d geometry for the Web UI, with a live editor. |
| `@d0nj/dsh-git-bash` | A working `bash` tool on W

indows, backed by Git Bash, beside the shipped `pwsh` tool. |
| `@d0nj/dsh-agent-rules` | `AGENTS.md
` as binding system-prompt sections, replacing the advisory reminder that agents can talk themselves

out of. |
| `@d0nj/dsh-browser` | A real Chrome window for the agent: the `browser` tool opens page
s, reads them as numbered accessibility outlines, and clicks, types and scrolls by ref. |
## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or newer
- pnpm 12
- A `dsh` installation on `PATH`

`pnpm build` is what produces the files a profile loads. Turbo caches it, so a change to one package
rebuilds only that package and its dependents.
## Adding a plugin
1. `packages/<name>/` with a `package.json` declaring `dsh.bundle.patch`, plus `cordis.patch.yml`, `

locale/en.json`, and `icon.svg`.
2. `src/index.ts` exporting `apply`, and optionally `Config` / `inj

ect`.
3. `tsconfig.build.json` extending `../../tsconfig.base.json`.
4. `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`
, then install it into a profile.

A linked directory install picks up rebuilt files, but the Host runs in-process, so a module change
needs a restart before the new code loads.
## Releasing
Bump the package's `version` in `package.json` and merge to `main`. The publish workflow then verifi
es the workspace, uploads every manifest version the npm registry does not have yet, and creates the
matching `<package>@<version>` tag. Pushing that tag by hand still works, and a push carrying no ne
w version publishes nothing.
Publishing uses npm OIDC trusted publishing, so no registry token is stored here. The first version
of a new package still has to be published once by hand, because trusted publishing cannot create a
package still has to be published once by hand, because trusted publishing cannot create a package.
## Dependency updates
`.github/renovate.json5` groups the Harness packages into a single "DeepSeek Harness" pull request a
nd rewrites `peerDependencies` together with `devDependencies`. That pairing matters: the Host refus
es to load a bundle whose declared `dsh-*` peers do not satisfy its own version, and Dependabot does
not update `peerDependencies` at all.
The config only runs once the Renovate app is installed on this repository. Bump the package version
in the pull request it opens; merging publishes the release.
